stem: High-risk HPV types such as 16 and 18 can cause which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: Hepatocellular carcinoma following chronic liver infection
options.misconception: Confuses HPV with the hepatitis viruses that cause liver cancer.
options.explanation: Hepatocellular carcinoma after chronic liver infection is linked to hepatitis B and C viruses, not HPV.

options.label: B
options.text: Cervical cell abnormalities that are precursors to cancer
options.misconception: None — high-risk HPV causes precancerous cervical abnormalities and anogenital cancers.
options.explanation: CDC: high-risk HPV types, including 16 and 18, cause cervical cell abnormalities that are precursors to cancer, and anogenital cancers.

options.label: C
options.misconception: Confuses HPV with HHV-8, the cause of Kaposi sarcoma.
options.explanation: Kaposi sarcoma is caused by human herpesvirus 8, mainly in people with HIV or other immunosuppression.

options.label: D
options.text: Adult T-cell leukemia after retroviral infection
options.misconception: Confuses HPV with HTLV-1, an oncogenic retrovirus.
options.explanation: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma follows infection with HTLV-1, a retrovirus that infects CD4 T cells.

options.label: E
options.text: Burkitt lymphoma arising from infected B cells
options.misconception: Confuses HPV with Epstein-Barr virus, which is linked to Burkitt lymphoma.
options.explanation: Burkitt lymphoma is linked to Epstein-Barr virus, which infects B cells; HPV infects squamous epithelium.

context: Learning objective: High-risk HPV types, including 16 and 18, cause cervical cell abnormalities that are precursors to cancer, and anogenital cancers.
